course_name_original: ANTENNE, PROPAGAZIONE E CIRCUITI AD ALTA FREQUENZA
course_name_en: ANTENNAS, PROPAGATION AND HIGH FREQUENCY CIRCUITS

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the basic notions of electromagnetic wave radiation and the application of fundamental electromagnetism theorems.
Knowledge and understanding of the basic notions of antenna operation: characteristic parameters in transmission and reception, antenna efficiency.
Knowledge and understanding of the basic notions of electromagnetic wave propagation in guiding structures.
Ability to perform the analysis of simple radiating systems.
Ability to design a link between antennas.
Ability to use an electromagnetic simulator for RFID system design.
Ability to understand the physical feasibility of an antenna system.
Ability to logically present complex demonstrations for the calculation of the radiated and/or guided electromagnetic field.
Ability to independently find documentation related to antenna characterization.

syllabus_topics: Characterization of an antenna system and definition of its characteristic parameters
Analysis and design of RFID systems
Theory of electromagnetic potentials: vector and scalar potential, Lorentz condition, homogeneous vectorial and scalar Helmholtz equations and their solutions
Field generated by an arbitrary source distribution
Wire antennas in transmission: Hallen's integral equation, input impedance, effective height, directivity, gain, radiation efficiency
Wire antennas in reception: effective height in reception, effective area
Aperture antennas: rectangular aperture with uniform illumination
Separation of transverse field components from longitudinal components
Coaxial cable and connection between electromagnetic and circuit approach
Transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes
Analogy between guided propagation and transmission lines
Laboratory: Design, realization and characterization of an RFID tag
teaching_methods: Ex cathedra lecture at the blackboard

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (discussion of laboratory work and questions on program parts)

assessment_rules: The oral exam starts with a discussion of the laboratory work to verify the candidate's ability to apply acquired notions. This is followed by further questions on all parts of the program. Grades range from insufficient (negative due to serious conceptual errors) to 29-30 cum laude (excellent, complete, in-depth knowledge, originality, and rigor). Laude is awarded for brilliant and original work.

G. Conciauro, Introduzione alle onde elettromagnetiche, McGraw-Hill. (fundamental laws and theorems, guides, antennas)
R. E. Collin, Antennas and radiowave propagation, 1985. (antennas)
S. Ramo, J. R. Whinnery, T. Van Duzer, Campi e onde nell’elettronica per le comunicazioni, Franco Angeli Ed. (fundamental laws and basic concepts)
